source: The President, post of Dec 8, 2025, as kept by the American Presidency Project
text: The President writes that the United States will allow Nvidia to ship its H200 chips to approved customers in China. The post gives no number of chips.
words: the United States will allow NVIDIA to ship its H200 products to approved customers in China

source: Nvidia, quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 26, 2026
text: Nvidia's later quarterly report says the US government began granting licences in February 2026, for what it calls "small amounts" of H200 products to named customers in China.
words: Beginning in February 2026, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers

source: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Senate hearing (Rev's transcript)
text: The Commerce Secretary, asked in the Senate how many H200 chips had been licensed, answers that none has been sold yet. He calls it his understanding. The words are from a commercial transcript. The committee's own page for the hearing offers the video and his prepared remarks, and no transcript.
words: So we have not sold them chips as of yet. / That's my understanding as I sit here with you today.

source: Reuters, May 14, 2026, as carried by MarketScreener
text: Reuters, from unnamed people: the Commerce Department has approved about 10 Chinese companies to buy the H200, each "up to 75,000 chips", and "not a single delivery has been made so far".
words: The U.S. Commerce Department has approved around 10 Chinese companies including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com to purchase Nvidia's H200 chips / each approved customer can purchase up to 75,000 chips under the U.S. licensing terms / not a single delivery has been made so far

source: Nvidia, results call of May 20, 2026 (the transcript on its investor site)
text: Nvidia says on its results call that the US government has approved licences for the H200, that it has made no revenue from them yet, and that it does not know whether imports will be allowed.
words: While the US government has approved licenses for H200 to be shipped to China-based customers, we have yet to generate any revenue, and we are uncertain whether any imports will be allowed into the country.

source: Reuters, Jul 14, 2026, as carried by Investing.com
text: The under secretary of commerce for industry and security tells the House Foreign Affairs Committee that shipments have begun and are "very few", as Reuters reports.
words: There have been minimal exports of any H200s to China so far / He said shipments of H200 chips have begun but the number was "very few."

source: Nvidia, quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter to Jul 26, 2026
text: Nvidia's quarterly report: it has "made a fraction of the allowed shipments", and those shipments are "less than 1% of Data Center revenue" for the quarter. The same report gives Data Center revenue as $89.0 billion.
words: Those shipments account for less than 1% of Data Center revenue in our most recent quarter. / we have made a fraction of the allowed shipments under the USG's H200 licensing program

source: Nvidia, results call for the quarter ended Oct 25, 2026 (the transcript on its investor site)
text: Nvidia says on its results call that its sales of licensed Hopper Data Center products to China in the quarter were $2.4 billion. Its commentary on the quarter gives the same sum, and Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion. Reuters, reporting the call, says the quarter ended Oct 25 and that the Hopper family includes the H200. Nvidia's quarterly report (Form 10-Q) for this quarter was not yet filed when looked for on Nov 23, 2026.
words: Q3 sales of licensed Hopper Data Center products to China was $2.4 billion.

source: Nvidia, results call for the quarter ended Oct 25, 2026 (the transcript on its investor site)
text: On the same call Nvidia says it is no longer shipping these products to China and that its guidance includes none. It gave no reason. Reuters wrote that its then interim chief executive "did not explain why Nvidia had stopped shipping the processors or whether the halt would be permanent".
words: we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper Data Center products to China / Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper Data Center products included

source: The licence table, H200 License and Equivalent Application Status as of May 11, 2026, made public by the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Nov 19, 2026
text: The House Foreign Affairs Committee makes public, by unanimous consent and under its chairman's powers, the table of licence applications for Nvidia's H200 and AMD's MI325X, with their status on May 11, 2026, from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security. Every approved application is marked "Approved, not shipped". An application names a data-centre operator or ultimate consignee; it is not an order, and an approval there is Washington's licence, not Beijing's. The committee says the summary does not show every application in full; for example, Nvidia applied on Dec 19, 2025 "to export 445,000 H200s to Tencent". The table's only Tencent row of that date is for 75,000, approved; neither document says whether it is that application.
words: H200 License and Equivalent Application Status as of May 11, 2026 / Approved, not shipped
